q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
The data doesn't match the question: ROAS rose and net profit improved (got less negative), not the other way round. Over the last 30 days (2026-09-16..2026-10-15) net ROAS moved from 0.73x to 0.95x, and net profit improved from ₹-5,51,581 to ₹-54,659 — so ROAS up and net profit also up (less loss).

Why that happened (largest effects first)
- Lower ad spend lifted ROAS: daily ad spend fell ~19.8% (from about ₹47,393 to ₹38,025), which reduces ad cost per order and raised net ROAS even though sales also declined. This is the biggest mechanical lever behind the ROAS increase.  
- Contribution margin fell less than ad spend: contribution margin moved down (~₹47,101 → ₹43,452, -7.7%), so the drop in costs (ad spend) outpaced the drop in margin and improved net profit.  
- Volume and unit economics moved mildly: orders and AOV were modestly lower (orders down ~5.1%, AOV down ~9.3%), so sales fell, but not enough to offset the ad spend reduction.  
- No single causal event found in the data: the diagnosis did not identify a supported cause that statistically explains both movements (several candidate drivers were tested and excluded or labelled insufficient evidence).

Worth checking: drill ad spend and contribution margin by platform/campaign (Meta vs Google vs organic) to see whether the ad cuts are concentrated in low-ROAS places or were a broad reduction.
